https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USB_On-The-Go

Use of USB OTG allows those devices to switch back and forth between the roles of host and device.

USB OTG introduces the concept of a device performing both master and slave roles ...

USB OTG defines two roles for devices: OTG A-device and OTG B-device, specifying which side supplies power to the link, and which initially is the host. The OTG A-device is a power supplier, and an OTG B-device is a power consumer. In the default link configuration, the A-device acts as a USB host with the B-device ...

All this means is that the USB chip in your phone, at a minimum needs to be able to function in host/master mode AND supply power. Changing from master to slave on the fly, and be fully compliant with OTG would be the cherry on top.
